name: SessionBench + Resident-Slot SLA (benchmark-first, Wafer-motion session serving)
one_line: A benchmark-first company that publishes the sessions-per-GPU standard (SessionBench), ships the residency runtime that wins it, and sells warm session-slots with a stated retention window per slot-hour into voice and agent platforms that already price by concurrency — the Wafer engagements-plus-dedicated-endpoints motion applied to session-shaped serving, engine-neutral and upstream of candidates A/B/C.

numeric_claims.claim: Repo's own estimate: ~2 GPU-hours per arm-D tuning idea; N=300 runs take ~3,240 s
LMCache CPU offload/restore in vLLM 0.24 (Qwen2.5-7B, A100): 4k cold 301 ms → restore 30 ms (10.0x); 16k 1,320 → 77 ms (17.1x); 16,384 tokens retrieved in 39.8 ms at 22.0 GB/s; single request only
vLLM prefix-cache hit vs cold TTFT: ~12x at 4k (280→24 ms), 25–34x at 16k (1,250→45 ms); ≥32k crashed vLLM V1 EngineCore in 3 configs
HF pinned-CPU restore vs HF re-prefill 11.8x at 4k → 28.9x at 64k (Qwen2.5-7B, A100); combined 10–34x single-request headline
Dexa disk-backed connector: 8B/A100/8k resume 1681 ms vs vLLM cold 617 ms (0.37x); 24×3072 async P99 8,930 vs vanilla 5,596 ms; 16×8192 P99 20,296 vs 9,379 ms

Reconciliation (derived): restore wins iff tier bandwidth × vLLM prefill time > KV bytes; pinned RAM 10–20 GB/s crosses over below 4k, disk <1 GB/s only near 64k; RAM-tier restore at 16k–64k under concurrency unmeasured
fp8 (e4m3) and int8 KV at 0.5x bytes: 100% greedy agreement over 48 tokens; int4 29%
Cross-instance resume: two vLLM processes sharing a Volume, identical_output=True, 8176/8192 tokens matched; TP=1 only
DexaConnector conformance: 10/10 KVConnectorBase_V1 hook signatures match vLLM 0.24.0

Residency cost model (modeled, not measured): 6.0x/4.9x/2.0x cheaper at 2/15/120 min idle (64k, 50 turns); break-even idle 4k: HBM 1 min, RAM 6 min, NVMe 33 min; 64k: 2 min, 11 min, 4.9 hr; assumed GPU $1.80/hr, RAM $0.006/GB-hr, NVMe $0.0002/GB-hr
$0.006 per slot-hour illustration = $1.80/hr ÷ 300 sessions (assumed A100-class rate from the cost model, not an L40S quote; L40S pricing not in research files)

founder_decisions.decision: Neutral benchmark vs. owning the winning engine
founder_decisions.options: Strictly neutral SessionBench with a separately sold runtime; benchmark as marketing for our runtime; benchmark-only business (certification and engagements)
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: It is a positioning and trust judgment; the Week-2 cross-engine run informs it (if an OSS stack wins, neutrality is cheap; if ours wins, neutrality costs revenue) but does not decide it

founder_decisions.options: Voice (only measured knee: 2.5k-token sessions on L40S, 1.5x at seed 1); agents (public telemetry from TraceLab/Codex traces but zero in-engine evidence above 16k); both
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: It is a market-selection judgment; the founder asked that no market-size judgments be made — the two Week-2 profiles supply the technical evidence only

founder_decisions.decision: Upstream (platforms/providers) vs. downstream (end builders, i.e. candidate B)
founder_decisions.options: Sell to LiveKit/Inworld/ElevenLabs/Deepgram-class platforms and to inference providers; sell directly to voice-agent builders; both
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: Depends on where LLM spend sits (Inworld models LLM <5% of a minute, Retell's LLM line is 4–65%) and on channel conflict with platforms — a commercial judgment the discovery calls inform

founder_decisions.decision: Engagements + dedicated endpoints (Wafer) vs. software/BYOC (Tensormesh Operator model) vs. OSS harness + paid certification
founder_decisions.options: Wafer motion; Tensormesh-style software with a 30%-of-savings or per-slot price; open harness with paid certification and support
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: Business-model choice; evidence that informs it is whether partners can and will run the harness themselves and whether they prefer buying capacity or software

founder_decisions.options: L40S/46 GB where the measured wall exists; H100/80 GB where derived (unrun) arithmetic suggests the baseline cliff moves to ~N 400–450; B200-class where nothing is measured
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: Both repos name the larger-HBM GPU as the top threat to the thesis and measured nothing there; the H100 gate produces the evidence, the founder weighs it against the fleet the customers actually run

founder_decisions.decision: Model class to benchmark and serve
founder_decisions.options: 7B fp16 dense (everything measured); 26–35B dense/A3B MoE that platforms actually run (LiveKit 31B, Inworld 26B, ElevenLabs 35B-A3B); 300B+ MoE
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: KV geometry and prefill speed change the knee and the tier break-evens; one 31B/A3B rerun gives the number, the founder picks the catalog

founder_decisions.options: vLLM KVConnector V1 (experimental API, port cost from 0.9.2 to 0.28 unknown); SGLang RFC #27574 Pin-with-TTL path (open, unimplemented); Dynamo KVBM retention semantics; support all three
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: Strategic bet on which ecosystem lands session hints first; port cost and RFC status are the evidence

founder_decisions.decision: Sell retention as a guarantee (with SLA credits) or as a target with published metrics
founder_decisions.options: Guaranteed warm-for-T with credits; best-effort with transparent honor rate; tiered (HBM guaranteed, RAM/NVMe best-effort)
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: Risk appetite; the honor-rate gate (≥99% proceeds) supplies the measurement but not the liability decision

founder_decisions.decision: Whether Tensormesh's, llm-d's, Wafer's, Dynamo's or the SGLang RFCs' adjacency matters
founder_decisions.options: Treat as validation of demand; treat as future competition; treat as acquisition/partnership channels (Wafer received acquisition offers from cloud/inference providers)
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: The founder explicitly reserved 'already exists' judgments; §9 states the facts neutrally

founder_decisions.decision: Open-source the harness (Apache) or keep it proprietary
founder_decisions.options: Apache-2.0 harness with proprietary runtime; fully proprietary; harness open but trace profiles/real-trace converters proprietary
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: Licensing strategy; evidence is whether platforms require neutrality and self-runnability before they trust a leaderboard
